model_annotation: This plot illustrates the accuracy (ACC) of multiple methods as a function of co-occurrence number, presented in a three-dimensional perspective view. The x-axis represents "Co-occurrence Number" on a logarithmic scale, spanning from approximately 10¹ to 10³. The y-axis represents "ACC (%)" on a linear scale, ranging from 0 to 65, with tick marks at intervals of 5 percentage points. Six lines are shown, each corresponding to a different method as indicated in the legend. The "Base" line (black with circular markers, solid) starts at roughly 35% at the lowest co-occurrence number and shows a declining trend, dropping to negative or near-zero values at higher co-occurrence numbers. The "FT" line (blue with triangular markers, solid) begins around 5–10% and similarly decreases across the x-axis range. The "IKE" line (red with cross/plus markers, solid) starts near 35–38% and gradually declines to approximately 15–20% at the highest co-occurrence values. The "MEND" line (brown with arrow/dash markers, solid) begins around 35% and decreases to roughly 20% across the range. The "MEMIT" line (purple with square markers, solid) starts near 35% and declines to approximately 15% at the highest co-occurrence number. The "ROME" line (green with diamond markers, solid) starts at the highest values among all methods, approximately 46–47%, and shows a gradual decline to around 25% at the largest co-occurrence number, remaining consistently above the other lines throughout the plotted range.
